candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies client-needs subcategory (13–19% of items); this item tests medication laboratory monitoring and recognition of serious adverse effects during chronic therapy.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Laboratory and symptom monitoring for serious medication-induced hepatic injury
candidate.educational_objective: Monitor oral dantrolene therapy with baseline and interval liver-function assessment and prompt evaluation of symptoms suggesting hepatic injury because clinically important hepatotoxicity can occur during treatment.

options.A: Obtain baseline liver-function studies and repeat hepatic-function testing at appropriate intervals while monitoring for symptoms of hepatitis or jaundice
options.B: No hepatic assessment is needed because oral dantrolene is not associated with clinically important liver injury
options.C: Monitor only cardiac rhythm because liver toxicity is unrelated to long-term dantrolene therapy
options.D: Assume normal baseline liver tests permanently exclude later hepatotoxicity

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed labeling for oral dantrolene contains a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity, including fatal and nonfatal symptomatic hepatitis. The warnings section states that liver-function studies are desirable at the start of therapy to establish a baseline and should be repeated at appropriate intervals. If symptoms compatible with hepatitis occur together with abnormal liver tests or jaundice, dantrolene should be discontinued. B and C contradict the boxed warning and monitoring instructions. D is incorrect because liver injury can develop after therapy begins even when pretreatment studies are not abnormal.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The current official oral-dantrolene label directly supports baseline and interval hepatic monitoring and recognition of symptomatic hepatitis/jaundice because of potentially serious hepatotoxicity.
candidate.source_locator: DailyMed current Dantrolene Sodium Capsules label → Boxed Warning: dantrolene has potential for hepatotoxicity and symptomatic hepatitis, including fatal cases, has been reported; use with appropriate hepatic-function monitoring. Warnings: obtain liver-function studies at the start of therapy as a baseline; repeat liver-function studies at appropriate intervals; if symptoms compatible with hepatitis occur with abnormal liver tests or jaundice, discontinue therapy.
candidate.source_organization: National Library of Medicine (DailyMed; FDA-approved prescribing information)
candidate.stem: A client receives oral dantrolene for chronic spasticity. Which monitoring plan is supported by the current prescribing information?
